articles.title: Carbon Raw
articles.summary: Fine micro-weave carbon-like surface, semi-matte with slight sparkle, subtle depth in the pattern. Reads as a flat colour with a barely visible fine checker grain; at distance it is just a plain satin panel in whatever colour you give it.
articles.what: Up close: A flat neutral-grey preview with a very faint soft checkerboard of 12-14 px squares, like a plain-weave carbon cloth under a haze. Contrast is tiny, and there are no highlights or colour; the grey is only the placeholder input. From a distance: Reads as a flat colour with a barely visible fine checker grain; at distance it is just a plain satin panel in whatever colour you give it. Measured spec (average): metal 131, roughness 157, coat 200. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Carbon Raw on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, mirrors, spoilers: classic carbon placement
Splitters and diffusers: dry-carbon look
Numbers read in most colours since the base is quiet; just keep contrast against the colour you pick.
Stripes, panels and large graphics: the quiet base takes any overlay
Pairs well with: gloss black, red, yellow, titanium.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a black carbon fibre look by itself: the preview is grey, and the colour is whatever you pick
Not glossy wet carbon: it is semi-matte with dull clearcoat
Avoid: busy graphics hide the weave, scaled too small it reads as flat grey.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 131 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 157 (semi-matte), clearcoat 200 (almost no clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: busy graphics hide the weave, scaled too small it reads as flat grey.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes, panels and large graphics: the quiet base takes any overlay; gradient fades: the flat weave takes any gradient cleanly
Patterns to avoid: other carbon, weave or checker patterns: they cause moire with the fine checks
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat patches: add a wet carbon-under-clear look; metallic flake spec: adds sparkle the base lacks
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
